title: wt session list --json
description: The Claude sessions in a worktree, or in every worktree of the repository. Printed by `wt session list [<work>] --json` as the only thing on stdout; it writes nothing to any session. Schema 1: fields may be added and enumerations may gain values; nothing is renamed or removed. See docs/json.md.

sessions.description: The worktree's sessions, the one that needs its person first and then the newest, the session wt runs under last.

sessionsError.description: Why claude's sessions could not be read (claude is not on the PATH, it did not answer). The sessions are then empty and the exit status is 1.

error.description: Why the worktree could not be found, or is ambiguous.

session.description: One Claude session in a worktree, as wt list's SESSION column knows it, with where a message to it would go.

kind.description: Whose session: always claude; Codex sessions take no messages and are not listed.

id.description: The short id claude attach takes; null for a session open only in a terminal.

sessionId.description: The conversation's full id: what --expect-session takes.

name.description: The name the session goes by, cleaned of control characters; null when it has none.

pid.description: Claude's process; null for a session with none, a parked background one.

terminal.description: Open in a terminal: an interactive session, or a background one attached there.

state.description: As everywhere in wt: idle is a session waiting for its person; anything else, and anything not known to be idle, is busy.

claudeState.description: claude agents --json's state (working, blocked, done, failed, stopped), raw; null for a session with none.

claudeStatus.description: claude agents --json's status (busy, waiting, idle), raw; null while it has no process.

waitingFor.description: What a waiting session waits on (permission prompt, input needed), raw; null unless it is.

inbox.description: The inbox's socket, as uds: without the prefix: an absolute path. Null when inboxUnavailable says why.

inboxUnavailable.description: Why there is no inbox. notRunning: no process. own: the session wt runs under; wt does not send to it. codex: reserved, Codex sessions are not listed. noRegistry: claude's registry file for the pid is missing, unreadable, or names another session. notASocket: the path is not a socket of yours in a directory closed to others. refused: it did not accept a connection.

transcript.description: The session's transcript file, when one is found.

shown.description: The session wt list shows for its worktree.
